choices.label: The number of paths reaching that column in the row being processed.
choices.feedback: The table counts paths, so multiple ways of reaching the same cell must be retained.

questions.prompt: Where do paths into an interior cell come from?

choices.label: The cells below and to the right.
choices.feedback: Allowed moves are down and right, so incoming path counts from above and left are added.

choices.label: Only the neighboring cell with more paths.

questions.prompt: Which values should “i” visit, and in what order?

choices.label: Option D

questions.prompt: What should “row[j]” store after this step?

choices.label: Option A
choices.feedback: Add “row[j - 1]” to “row[j]”.

choices.label: Option B
choices.feedback: This uses “row[j] += row[(j + 1)]” instead of “row[j] += row[j - 1]”. On this test, it raises IndexError: list index out of range; the expected result is 28.

choices.label: Option C
choices.feedback: This uses “row[j] += row[(j * 1)]” instead of “row[j] += row[j - 1]”. On this test, it returns 4; the expected result is 28.

choices.label: Option D
choices.feedback: This uses “row[j] += row[(j // 1)]” instead of “row[j] += row[j - 1]”. On this test, it returns 4; the expected result is 28.
